deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is folio 83r of the essay '3. Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' (dated 1 March 1853 on the previous page). The essay was printed posthumously in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876, Nachlass section). The page has three parts.

(A) Metaphysical hypothesis and gravitation. Riemann proposes that in every ponderable atom 'Stoff' (a space-filling aether) continually passes from the corporeal world into the 'Geisteswelt'. The marginal note specifies that each atom absorbs per unit time an amount of Stoff proportional to its gravitational mass. He also cites Herbartian psychology: each individual representation, not the soul, has substantiality.

He recalls that gravitation is fully determined in any region by the potential function P of all ponderable masses there. Equivalently, P is a function of position such that the mass enclosed by a closed surface S is (1/4π)∮ ∂P/∂p dS. This is Gauss's flux theorem, i.e. ΔP = -4πρ for P = Σ m/r, with p the normal direction.

He then assumes the aether is an incompressible, homogeneous fluid without inertia, and that each atom swallows equal amounts in equal times, proportional to its mass. Implicit step (mine): incompressibility gives div v = -k ρ_mass. The flux of v through S is therefore -k·(enclosed mass), so one may take v = (k/4π)∇P. The aether velocity is thus proportional to the gravitational field strength.

The bracketed, query-marked sentence conjectures that the pressure (force) an atom experiences is proportional to the flow velocity at its location. Hence gravitation on an atom can be expressed through the pressure of the aether in its immediate neighbourhood, i.e. a contact-action, sink-model theory of gravity.

(B) Light. The aether must also propagate light and heat vibrations. For a linearly polarized ray, let x be the distance along the ray and y the elongation at time t. Because the propagation speed is very nearly constant (= α), the d'Alembert solution y = f(x+αt) + φ(x-αt) holds very nearly, i.e. y_tt = α² y_xx.

Integrating once in time (step mine), exact validity is equivalent to ∂y/∂t = α² ∫^t ∂²y/∂x²(x,τ) dτ, with the lower limit and integration function suppressed.

Riemann then generalizes to a hereditary (memory) law: ∂y/∂t = α² ∫^t ∂²y/∂x²(x,τ) φ(t-τ) dτ. The kernel φ need not equal 1 for all t-τ > 0; it may decay as t-τ → ∞. It only needs to stay close to 1 over a sufficiently long interval to agree with experience. With φ ≡ 1 the wave equation is recovered. As an illustration (mine), an exponential kernel e^{-(t-τ)/T} gives y_tt = α² y_xx - y_t/T, a damped wave (telegraph) equation.

(C) Start of a continuum-kinematics set-up for the next page. Particle positions at time t are (x,y,z) relative to point O. Positions at an earlier time t' are (x',y',z') relative to O', so x',y',z' are functions of x,y,z. The next page uses this to diagonalize ds'² against ds², obtaining principal dilatations, and builds a viscoelastic aether with memory kernels ψ, φ.
errors: Sign convention: with P = Σ m/r, ∮ ∂P/∂n dS over the outward normal equals -4π M. So (1/4π)∮ ∂P/∂p dS = M requires p to be the inward normal, or P taken with the opposite sign. Riemann does not specify.
The time-integrated wave equation ∂y/∂t = α²∫^t y_xx dτ omits the lower limit and an additive function of x. It is equivalent to the wave equation only up to this integration term.
The symbol φ is used both for the second d'Alembert profile φ(x-αt) and for the memory kernel φ(t-τ), a notational clash.

The physical step from 'incompressible fluid without inertia' to 'pressure on the atom ∝ local flow velocity' is unjustified, and Riemann himself brackets it with a question mark. For a fluid with no inertia, Bernoulli/momentum arguments (such as the Lagally force on a sink, ρQU) are not available. The link needs some resistive or other mechanism.

results.what: Mass enclosed by closed surface = (1/4π)∮ ∂P/∂p dS (potential determines gravitation)
results.modern_name: Gauss's law for gravity / Poisson equation

results.what: Gravitation explained by an incompressible aether flowing into atoms (sinks) at rates proportional to mass, with force ∝ local flow velocity
results.usually_credited_to: Precursors: Fatio, Le Sage, Euler-type aether theories. Riemann's version is known from the Werke (1876).

results.what: d'Alembert solution y = f(x+αt) + φ(x-αt) for transverse light vibrations
results.modern_name: d'Alembert's solution of the 1D wave equation

results.what: Replacing the wave equation by y_t = α²∫^t y_xx(τ)φ(t-τ)dτ with a slowly decaying memory kernel
results.modern_name: Hereditary / memory-kernel (viscoelastic) wave equation; Volterra integro-differential equation
results.usually_credited_to: Boltzmann (1874) for hereditary elasticity, Volterra (1909-1913) for hereditary mechanics. Maxwell (1867) for viscoelastic relaxation.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is part of Riemann's 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie', printed in his Gesammelte Werke (1876) and discussed by historians. The memory-kernel wave equation anticipates Boltzmann and Volterra, but this anticipation is already known from the published text.

checkable.sympy: x,t,a=symbols('x t a'); f=Function('f'); g=Function('g'); y=f(x+a*t)+g(x-a*t); simplify(diff(y,t,2)-a**2*diff(y,x,2))==0
checkable.asserts: The d'Alembert form satisfies the wave equation y_tt = α² y_xx.
The potential of a point mass is harmonic away from the mass, so flux contributions come only from enclosed masses.
Outward flux of ∇(1/r) through a sphere is -4π, so (1/4π)∮∂P/∂p dS = mass requires the inward normal.

checkable.sympy: t,tau,T,a,x=symbols('t tau T a x',positive=True); u=Function('u'); Y=a**2*Integral(u(x,tau)*exp(-(t-tau)/T),(tau,-oo,t)); simplify(diff(Y,t)-(a**2*u(x,t)-Y/T))==0
checkable.asserts: With kernel φ = exp(-(t-τ)/T) and u = y_xx, y_t = Y satisfies y_tt = α² y_xx - y_t/T (damped wave equation). With φ≡1 (T→∞) the wave equation is recovered.

transcription_corrections: The first integral should read ∂y/∂t = αα ∫^t ∂²y/∂x² dτ. The image is faint but the published Werke text has the second x-derivative.
Marginal note '((Siehe Ende der Zugabe[?]))': the reading is uncertain in the image and may be '(Siehe Rede der Zugabe)'. Keep it marked as doubtful.
'nahezu[?] sehr nahe erfüllt': the image appears to show a struck-out word followed by 'sehr nahe erfüllt werden'.
'empfinden[?] wahrnehmen': the image seems to show 'Licht und Wärme empfinden', with 'wahrnehmen' as an alternative or correction.
